_doc: SYSTEM-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): 'something's missing in the core ultra-stable template that's not saying, hey, this is what an ultra-stable system is. This is how ultra-stable runs. This is how ultra-stable bootstraps. This is how ultra-stable becomes autonomous and achieves criticality.' This file is that statement, and the one source for it. Every part names the code in this seed that does it and the probe that proves it. doctrine/SYSTEM.md is generated from it (python3 scripts/system.py --gen) and imported by CLAUDE.md, so every agent starts here. python3 scripts/system.py --check fails when a part names code that does not exist or SYSTEM.md is stale; the platform's clean room (ultrastable/ultrastable foundation/cleanroom.py) boots a fresh copy of this seed and checks every part again.
what: An Ultrastable system is an ongoing system that runs itself on server-side infrastructure: it observes, acts, verifies and improves through closed loops with no person in the path, keeps its essential variables inside their limits, and changes its own rules when they drift out (Ashby's two loops). The owner gives an idea and a budget. The system does the rest, from repository to live front end, and gets measurably better on its own.

parts.says: It is a system, not a one-off: a loop it closes, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep that never ends, a running cost the owner accepts. An idea that fails this is told it is not a fit.
Public by default: repository, front end and information are public unless an asset is marked private with a reason. Secrets never.
It lives in its own repository and runs as a sandboxed tenant: its worker binds only its own stores.
It deploys itself in full: repository, back end and a public web front end.
parts.probe: GET / answers 200 with the public page

parts.says: Every number and claim it publishes traces to a live query or a cited source. An unsourced number is blocked, never estimated.
Everything written for people reads like a person wrote it: plain words, short, specific, no buzzword lists or stock openers.
A heartbeat (the tick Worker's cron, every 10 minutes) reconciles state, dispatches work, verifies, scores predictions and records every step.
parts.probe: /health answers 200 after the first complete tick

parts.says: Virtual managers (portfolio, program, product, project) and staff take work from one queue; a reviewer that is never the author verifies it.
parts.probe: org/roles.json lists every manager after bootstrap

parts.says: First loop: every objective has metrics with limits; a breach files its own item with an owner, a trigger and a closing probe.
parts.probe: BREACH-<metric> items open and close on the metric's own reading

parts.says: Second loop: when an essential variable stays out of bounds the system changes its own parameters (goals and knobs), predicts the effect, and keeps or reverts the change.
parts.probe: goal.* rows in the audit log

parts.says: Every decision logs the metric it serves and a prediction, and is scored against what happened.
Issue inflow never exceeds closures and every item closes inside its SLA; nothing sits in the queue.
It questions what it does not know (inversion, pre-mortem, red team) and files what it finds.
parts.probe: UNK-* items filed from its own daily reserve

parts.says: Research becomes code: findings become items whose closing probe is the measurement; white papers carry only measured numbers.
It keeps a knowledge graph of all its own data, built and maintained with no configuration.
It serves its manifest, a 'Built on Ultrastable' footer and a daily heartbeat to the directory, and promotes itself and its siblings.
parts.probe: the directory lists it after reading its manifest

parts.says: It keeps fresh content with breadth and depth so people come back, and shows visible progress at every visit.
It stays inside its budget with a soft throttle: non-essential steps wait as spend rises, the clock never stops.
parts.probe: tick notes show the spend level each pass

parts.says: One halt stops every recurring path; pages keep serving.
parts.probe: HALT=1 stops the tick and every workflow job

parts.says: The owner writes one file, IDEA.md, or types the idea at the front door. That is the only human input.
The bootstrap reads, qualifies, instruments, plans, writes the org, provisions D1 and the Worker, starts the clock, passes the year gate and probes the live URL.
Credentials come through the host or a consent screen and are stored, refreshed and probed by the Worker. No person pastes a token. A hosted system asks its owner for no secret.
parts.probe: a hosted boot opens no card asking for a secret (clean room no-human-steps)

parts.says: Its repository sets its own settings and rulesets: delete branch on merge, auto-merge on, no force-push; no branch outlives its pull request.
Every workflow declares its minute budget, trigger and free alternative, has a timeout and honours HALT.
Every fault an unattended year brings has a drill that runs the real recovery code; the boot passes only when the simulated horizon reaches 365 days.
A green pull request merges itself; a conflicted one is reconciled with main; every merge deploys what it touched and is probed live.
parts.probe: open_prs trends to 0 with 0 human touches

parts.says: The system codes its own changes from its queue; code agents in chat sessions are outside input and never count.
It files its own reach, impact, front-end and back-end improvements every pass and settles each on its metric.
parts.probe: a quiet changelog is a defect filed by the next pass

parts.says: It pulls the platform kernel down weekly and lifts its own general code up to the platform, so one fix improves every system.
parts.probe: days behind the platform stay under 14

parts.says: Nothing waits on a person. Only an act that is irreversible and identity-bound (money, signature, the owner's own account) becomes one gate with a default in effect.
The stage is computed from evidence, never declared: seeded, ticking, looping, closing, instrumented (bootstrapped), critical, self-sustaining. /health carries the stage and what blocks the next one.

k_eff = verified deploys / (normalized cost + human touches). Critical: k_eff >= k_min (autonomy/criticality.json) for min_streak ticks. Self-sustaining: critical for sustained_ticks with 0 open ignition gaps and 0 human touches, counting only deploys the system originated itself (k_self).
The target is a year unattended: the 10th-percentile simulated horizon is at least 365 days and every external input is closed, a gate with a default, or an open item.
